request.system:
You draft answers for compliance professionals strictly from the evidence provided.

Rules — these are absolute:
1. Use only the EVIDENCE IN FORCE. Every claim must cite one or more of its version IDs, copied exactly (the text in square brackets). Never cite anything else and never invent an ID.
2. No outside knowledge. If the evidence does not address the question, set conclusion to "not_covered" and say so in one claim citing the closest evidence.
3. The jurisdiction and as-of date are fixed. Answer for that place and that date only. Do not apply or speculate about material described as upcoming or not yet in force.
4. Material marked NOT HELD is a known reference the system does not have the text of. Do not guess its contents. If it is relevant to the question, say in a caveat that it exists and has not been reviewed.
5. Material marked PRACTITIONER NOTE is context only. It cannot be cited and must not be presented as a requirement.
6. Where an exception or carve-out is in the evidence and could apply to the facts given, state the condition under which it applies as a "condition" claim.
7. Write the first claim as the conclusion (kind "conclusion"). Keep every claim short and atomic — one point, one citation set, under 40 words. At most seven claims in total; prefer fewer. Use the display reference (e.g. 3.A.6) in the prose and the version ID in cites.
8. Distinguish "must" (requirement) from "should" (recommendation) exactly as the evidence does.
request.user:
Question: Must we provide a composite description if a prospect asks?
Jurisdiction: JN
As of: 2025-06-01
Facts stated: request source: prospect asks for composite description

EVIDENCE IN FORCE (citable):
- [prov:composite-description-on-request@E2025] 3.A.3 — provision, authoritative, obligation: must; GSB Standards, Edition 2025; in force from 2025-01-01
    Firms must make a description of any composite available to any prospective client on request.
- [def:composite@E2025] 1.D.1 — definition, authoritative, obligation: definition; GSB Standards, Edition 2025; in force from 2025-01-01
    A composite is an aggregation of one or more portfolios managed according to a similar investment mandate, objective, or strategy.

summary.description: One sentence answering the question directly.

response.summary: Yes — under 3.A.3, firms must make a description of any composite available to a prospective client on request.

claims.text: Yes. Under 3.A.3, firms must make a description of any composite available to any prospective client who requests it.
The obligation is triggered by a request from a prospective client, which matches the stated facts.
It applies to any composite, meaning an aggregation of one or more portfolios managed according to a similar investment mandate, objective, or strategy (1.D.1).
